query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of grain boundaries through nanostructuring can increase the coercive field of single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloys.
generation.mechanism: Pinning of magnetic domain walls at grain boundaries, leading to increased coercive field
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased coercive field relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, potentially exceeding 100 Oe
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy with no nanostructuring
generation.boundary: Grain size < 100 nm, alloy composition within 10% of FeCoNi
generation.uncertainty: Effect of grain boundary density and distribution on coercive field, potential for other nanostructure-induced effects

falsification_experiment.design: Compare coercive fields of nanostructured and non-nanostructured single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloys
measurements: Coercive field via hysteresis loop measurement
Grain size via transmission electron microscopy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercive field of the nanostructured alloy is not significantly higher than that of the non-nanostructured alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
